backlog.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO = 0.1 and add a linear warmup schedule over the first 10% of training time to stabilize gradient growth.
backlog.title: Linear Warmup Schedule

backlog.spec: Replace fixed matrix learning rate with layerwise adjustments, scaling hidden state norms each epoch to balance training signal.
backlog.title: Layerwise Learning Rate

backlog.spec: Reduce DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 32 to lower per-layer gradients and allow for higher learning rates.
backlog.title: Reduced Batch Size

backlog.spec: Add gradient clipping at norm=1.0 to prevent unstable updates and improve convergence.
backlog.title: Gradient Clipping

backlog.spec: Tie embedding and projection weights to reduce model size and improve generalization on smaller contexts.
backlog.title: Weight Tying

backlog.spec: Implement cosine annealing LR decay with warm restarts to periodically reset the schedule.
backlog.title: Learning Rate Decay

backlog.spec: Increase optimizer steps per batch accumulation to 2, effectively doubling the batch size without OOM.
backlog.title: Gradient Accumulation

backlog.spec: Enable AMP with bfloat16 support and AMP gradient checkpointing to save memory and speed up training.
backlog.title: Mixed Precision Training

backlog.spec: Add a simple local response normalization layer to stabilize activations during training.
backlog.title: Local Response Normalization

backlog.spec: Add a learnable positional bias parameter in the attention mechanism to guide sequence order.
backlog.title: Learnable Positional Bias

backlog.spec: Apply causal masking to future tokens to enforce autoregressive training and improve convergence.
backlog.title: Masked Attention

backlog.spec: Normalize weight matrix initialization to ~0.1 instead of 1.0 to reduce gradient variance.
backlog.title: Weight Initialization Scaling

backlog.spec: Use native checkpointing or custom KV caching to reduce memory usage and allow larger effective batch sizes.
backlog.title: Gradient Checkpointing

backlog.spec: Reduce batch size dynamically if memory usage exceeds threshold, then gradually increase back later.
backlog.title: Dynamic Batch Size

backlog.spec: Implement Sparse MoE block to expand model capacity while keeping parameters efficient.
backlog.title: Sparse MoE

backlog.spec: Allow Adam to update beta2 for each layer based on local gradient statistics.
backlog.title: Adaptive Learning Rate

backlog.spec: Add a penalty term to the loss that discourages large parameter updates for unstable layers.
backlog.title: Learning Rate Penalty

backlog.spec: Modify gradient reconstruction to use sparse resolution to improve stability with small gradients.
backlog.title: Gradient Resolution Reconstruction

backlog.spec: Add dropout on attention logits to encourage diversification of feature representations.
backlog.title: Attention Dropout

backlog.spec: Use a learning rate that decreases only when performance metric shows improvement.
backlog.title: Dynamic Learning Rate

backlog.spec: Initialize Layer Norm parameters with small learning rate until initial layers stabilize.
backlog.title: Layer Norm Warmup

backlog.spec: Add lambda loss term to stabilize gradients by emphasizing important tokens.
backlog.title: Lambda Loss

backlog.spec: Implement step decay with 5 epochs of cooldown to reduce learning rate gradually.
backlog.title: Learning Rate Scheduler

backlog.spec: Scale learning rate by 1/sqrt(batch size) to stabilize training across different batch sizes.
backlog.title: Learning Rate Scaling

backlog.spec: Reduce attention scope to 16% of keys and values with per-layer routers.
backlog.title: Sparse Attention

backlog.spec: Use mixed precision gradient checkpointing to reduce memory footprint and improve VRAM utilization.
backlog.title: Mixed Precision Gradient Checkpointing

backlog.spec: Add batch normalization before the attention mechanism to stabilize feature learning.
backlog.title: Batch Normalization

backlog.spec: Trigger LR decay once every 3 epochs to periodically reduce learning rate and improve convergence.
backlog.title: Learning Rate Decay Step

backlog.spec: Add dropout in the final prediction layers to encourage robustness in the output distribution.
backlog.title: Prediction Dropout

backlog.spec: Accumulate gradients across all devices in a single step using a large intermediate buffer (if VRAM permits) or smaller steps with a global reduction. This decouples the step count from the batch size, allowing a larger effective step size. If exact unbatching is too memory-intensive, try halving the effective optimizer steps total (equivalent to halving TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE) to see if the risk/reward balance improves.
backlog.title: Unbatched Gradients (Chargeback)

backlog.spec: Replace Adam with a lightweight 'batch-free' optimizer like AdaBelief or AdaWN. These optimizers are specifically designed to stabilize small-batch training and eliminate the need for a large gradient accumulator, potentially improving val_bpb without the memory overhead of accumulated gradients.
backlog.title: Weight Decay on Laws (AdaBelief/AdaWN)

backlog.spec: Insert an extra transformer layer at the beginning of the forward pass (zero-initialized, standard shift-around) that simply passes data through (Identity or standard) to the first real layer. While usually detrimental, training this layer more aggressively is essentially a case of strategy. If the performance degrades, it can be removed. If it helps, it is added as a permanent change. The primary goal here is to figure out if a larger effective model size (via layers) improves val_bpb.
backlog.title: Redundant Interaction Layer

backlog.spec: Swap the 'Coefficient LR' (WARMUP_RATIO schedule) for a 'Reduced Weight LR' schedule. This forces the learning rate to decrease over time towards the final value, potentially yielding a sharper model. This is typically equivalent to staying at the baseline for longer.
backlog.title: Step-based Warmdown (Step scheduler)

backlog.spec: Insert a bridge layer at the top of the transformer, taking a single layer's output and using a standard Stone bridge to connect to the next layer, with no batch normalization in between. This reduces the dimension of the base input to the next layer, potentially making the model simpler and smaller.
backlog.title: Reduction by Layer of Bridge

backlog.spec: Use a 'NLL Loss with multiple labels' (MultiLabelSoftmax) instead of the current 'NLL Loss with single label' (SVM). This approach is typically used for classification tasks with multiple class labels and is expected to perform worse. If the performance does not degrade, it is added as a permanent change. If it helps, it is added as a permanent change. The primary goal here is to figure out if a larger effective model size (via layers) improves val_bpb.
backlog.title: NLL Loss with Multiple Labels

backlog.spec: Insert a small scalar lambda (e.g., 0.0001) into the loss function and multiply it with the current task loss. This is a regularization term that encourages lower losses globally but does not necessarily improve the model. If the performance degrades, it is removed. If it helps, it is added as a permanent change. The primary goal here is to figure out if a larger effective model size (via layers) improves val_bpb.
backlog.title: Lambda-scale Loss

backlog.spec: Enable gradient checkpointing (also known as activation checkpointing) to reduce VRAM usage at the cost of computation time. This allows for a larger DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE or more efficient optimizer steps. The primary goal here is to figure out if a larger effective model size (via layers) improves val_bpb.
backlog.title: Gradient Checkpointing (if time permits)

backlog.spec: Add attention dropout (e.g., 0.05 or 0.1) to the attention scores in the transformer. This reduces the risk of overfitting and is expected to be a standard practice. If the performance degrades, it is removed. If it helps, it is added as a permanent change. The primary goal here is to figure out if a larger effective model size (via layers) improves val_bpb.
backlog.title: Attention Drop

backlog.spec: Add a gradient penalty term with a constant of 1.0 (or a small scalar like 0.0001) to the loss function. This is a regularization term that encourages lower losses globally but does not necessarily improve the model. If the performance degrades, it is removed. If it helps, it is added as a permanent change. The primary goal here is to figure out if a larger effective model size (via layers) improves val_bpb.
backlog.title: Gradient Penalty (Gradient=1)

backlog.spec: Replace current step/Sigmoid warmdown with a 5-stage cosine annealing schedule using 7.5% budget. After each stage finishes, restart warmup to 0.1 and let LR climb back to max. This introduces curvature that often outperforms static shapes for small GPTs.
backlog.title: Cosine Annealing with Restart

backlog.spec: Switch Adam to use scaled momentum for accumulated gradients within a micro-batch, but reset every N steps. This stabilizes updates without significantly altering step behavior, potentially aiding convergence precision.
backlog.title: Adaptive Learning Rate (Accumulated)

backlog.spec: Before the first step, scale all initial weights by sqrt(box_size/ratio_current_batch_size). This compensates for smaller effective batch sizes by adjusting initial signal magnitude, independent of learning rate scaling.
backlog.title: Weight Initialization Scaling by Batch Ratio

backlog.spec: Apply per-token dropout on the final logits before argmax, using a vectorized mask generated from batch index and a learned scalar. This creates noise that regularizes the probability distribution without altering weights, improving generalization on noisy fits.
backlog.title: Prediction Dropout (Vectorized)

backlog.spec: For each layer, use a separate warmup curve for the residual stream and internal stream, with warmup defaults set to the current budget. This allows different streams to adapt at different rates, reducing early instability in sensitive pathways.
backlog.title: Layer Norm Warmup (Per-Stream)

backlog.spec: Add a term lambda * nll(P, Q) to the loss, where Q is the forecast and P is the ground truth. The lambda varies with batch size and is scaled appropriately. This additional term penalizes deviations from the distribution more strongly, improving alignment.
backlog.title: Lambda-scale Loss (nll)

backlog.spec: Apply gradient dropout on the attention matrix during backpropagation, but not during feedforward. This encourages the network to rely on more diverse pathways and prevents overfitting to a single attention pattern.
backlog.title: Attention Dropout (Mini-batch)

backlog.spec: Switch to gradient checkpointing for every transformer layer at the current batch size, compiled in graph mode. This adds recompute cost upfront but frees VRAM at moderate batch sizes, allowing for finer-grained optimization.
backlog.title: Gradient Checkpointing (Layer-wise)

backlog.spec: Reduce the learning rate by a factor of 0.9 every time the average training loss drops below a threshold. This ensures that the optimization continues when progress becomes smoother, rather than only when loss increases.
backlog.title: Learning Rate Decay Step (Dynamic)

cand.description: Shrink the sliding window of the short-attention layers from 50% to 16% of the context (about 327 keys). Every 4th layer and the last layer stay full-context. This is a fixed local-window approximation of sparse attention, with no learned per-layer routers, so it stays compatible with FA3.

memo:
Helped: halving TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**18 with LR scaled by sqrt(batch ratio) gave 1.0916 (-0.0230), the only accept. More optimizer steps in the fixed 300 s seems to matter. Doubling the batch to 2**20 was much worse (1.1820, +0.0674), which fits. Dropping DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 32 gave 1.0938 (+0.0022), so it did not help.

Did not help: schedule changes (cosine 1.1233, 0.1 warmup 1.1272, 5 cosine stages 1.1395, plateau decay 1.1000), per-layer Muon LR (1.1167), epsilon floor (1.1149), tied lm_head (1.1291), MoE (1.1089), extra layer (1.1148). Gradient clipping (1.1122) and 5-stage step decay (1.1111) looked slightly better, but each is a single run, so the gaps may be noise.

Next: try 2**17 batch with sqrt LR scaling. Retune LR scale and weight decay at the new batch size. Replicate 1.0916. Retry clipping at 1.0 on the new incumbent. Skip more LR-shape and architecture tinkering. Skip gradient checkpointing, which was aborted four times.
